svg.text: % of patients sequenced, by their highest sensitive level (in any cancer type)
Bars: each patient once, at their highest sensitive level; the right column is the share at levels 1–3B and the share with a resistance level (R1/R2) besides. Each patient's
highest OncoKB therapeutic level (v7.5, the pinned store) over the alterations in any of their samples in the cohort sequenced for mutations — called mutations and
high-level copy-number calls; the store holds no level for structural variants at this pin, so a fusion is never counted — and, separately, whether any alteration carries a
resistance level (R1, R2). The level is the store's highest for the alteration in ANY cancer type, not in the patient's own: an alteration actionable only elsewhere (PTEN or
PIK3CA, level 1 with capivasertib in breast cancer, in any other cancer) counts here, so these shares are an upper bound on what is actionable for these patients.
Denominator: patients with at least one sample in the cohort sequenced for mutations — “all patients”: 48,179 of 48,179. Panel-aware in the only way a level can be: a
gene their panel did not cover is unknown, not "no actionable alteration" — No level means none was found on the genes sequenced. Groups are CANCER_TYPE per
patient (Multiple (samples disagree) when their samples disagree); the 8 largest are drawn and the rest pooled into Other (“all patients”: 58 groups). Concordance:
patients with a sequenced sample whose SAMPLE_TYPE is Primary and one whose is Metastasis (matched case-insensitively), the highest level over each side's samples
compared — “all patients”: 2,278 patients, 25.5% discordant. A level present on one side only can be a real difference between the tumours, or a gene one side's panel
